title: Code Review & Collaboration
learning_objectives: Understand the purpose and benefits of code review for software quality
Leave constructive comments on GitHub PRs (line comments, review comments)
Use GitHub review tools: approve, request changes, comment
Apply code review best practices (kind, specific, actionable feedback)
Respond to review feedback professionally and implement requested changes
Push additional commits to update an open PR
Understand when a PR is ready to merge vs needs more work
outline: Introduction: Code review as quality gate and learning opportunity
Why code review matters: catching bugs, knowledge sharing, consistency
Types of review feedback: approve, request changes, comment
Leaving line comments: specific, actionable suggestions
Writing review comments: constructive tone, examples, alternatives
Code review best practices: compliment good work, suggest don't demand
Common review focus areas: logic errors, edge cases, readability, documentation
Responding to review feedback: gratitude, clarification, implementation
Pushing additional commits to update PR
Hands-on: Self-review exercise using CatchBook PR
Simulated peer review: reviewing your own PR with fresh eyes
When to merge: all checks pass, reviews approved, no unresolved threads

catchbook_context.feature: Code review culture for CatchBook quality assurance
catchbook_context.deliverable: Complete review cycle on CatchBook PR: receive feedback, make changes, update PR

criteria: Leave at least 3 constructive review comments on own PR (simulate reviewer)
Identify potential improvements in CatchBook documentation
Make changes based on simulated feedback
Push additional commits to update the open PR
Explain how code review improves CatchBook development velocity long-term
Demonstrate professional response to critical feedback (simulated scenario)

resources.title: How to Make Your Code Reviewer Fall in Love with You
Unlearning Toxic Behaviors in Code Review

professor_constraints: Model constructive review language ('Consider...', 'What if...', 'I wonder...')
Emphasize empathy: reviewer and author are on same team
Show examples of good vs bad review comments
Address imposter syndrome: everyone makes mistakes, review helps everyone learn
Connect to CatchBook: 'This review catches the bug before users see it'
Practice self-review as skill (reading your own code critically)
Avoid bikeshedding discussion (defer style debates to linters in Phase 2)
